observations: Key sorting is done on RAW (pre-NFC) keys, then keys are NFC-normalised for output, in both frozen scripts and in this module. Output key order is therefore not necessarily sorted post-NFC (e.g. the crafted sample: raw key 'e+combining acute' sorts before 'z' by code point, then normalises to 'é', so output order is a, é, z). Frozen keys are ASCII, so this has no effect on frozen hashes.
Canonical bytes have no trailing newline; evidence files append a single LF when writing, which is not part of the hashed bytes. Hashing is over UTF-8 bytes.

Environment variable VALUES cannot be scanned without knowing them; they are excluded structurally (no builder in src/canonical/ reads process.env) and the literals that would leak (repo root, $HOME, tmpdir, hostname) are scanned. A generic 'any absolute Unix path' rule is deliberately NOT included: fixture HTML legitimately contains '/' (tags, XPath), so it would false-positive; the exact leakable literals plus the Windows drive-letter rule cover the leak vector.

The username rule matches only in path/identifier context because the frozen fixtures legitimately contain 'root' inside 'shadowrootmode' (F022-F024); a bare-substring rule would false-positive on frozen data.
deviationsAndOpenItems: During development test:canonical initially failed 2/36: (1) the pid rule did not match the JSON-quoted key form {"pid":1234} (rule fixed to also match "pid":); (2) the Windows-path planted test string was over-escaped (double backslashes at run time, so the rule correctly did not match; test data fixed). Both were test/rule defects, not module defects; final run 36/36.

src/canonical/node-shims.d.ts was added because the project has no @types/node by design: it declares only node:crypto and node:os surfaces used by the canonical module. The shared src/node-builtins.d.ts was NOT modified. The module uses Uint8Array/TextEncoder (standard) instead of Buffer.
